newsitem.title: USA: Argentina needs fiscal handcuff, labor reform - Hanke.
newsitem.headline: Argentina needs fiscal handcuff, labor reform - Hanke.

text.p: Argentina has not gone far enough to reform its economy, and still needed to balance its public finances and to implement labor market reforms, U.S. private economist Steve Hanke said Wednesday.

Hanke, past advisor to Argentina's Economy Ministry and currency board guru, said Argentina had managed to restrain monetary policy through its convertibility system, but the country desperately need to restrain its fiscal accounts.
"We've got the handcuffs on monetary authorities with convertibility," Hanke told a conference. "I want to start handcuffing the fiscal authorities."
He called for Argentina to apply a New Zealand-style fiscal system, where government accounts were audited by independent agents according to international standards.
"Nothing in the structure of the fiscal set-up has been changed in Argentina," Hanke said. "A New Zealand type approach is the only thing that would work in Argentina."
Hanke also said the country needed to implement labor market reforms, and blamed the country's high unemployment rate, which stood at 16.1 percent in May, on inflexible labor conditions.
